stops.note: a backwoods countryman of São Paulo's interior, possibly from a Tupi word though the source is disputed; Monteiro Lobato's 1914 character Jeca Tatu fixed the stereotype
'little bumpkin', a rustic cachaça-lime-sugar drink that a popular story places around Piracicaba in São Paulo state; Brazilian Decree 4,851 of 2003 defines it in law as a typically Brazilian drink
spread through Brazilian bars abroad, and the International Bartenders Association lists it among its official cocktails

current_meaning: a Brazilian cocktail of cachaça, lime and sugar
